chapter_title: The Ascent and the Encounter with Jory
summary: Joe begins to deteriorate rapidly while ascending the stairs to his hotel room at the Meremont Hotel. His body weakens, his heart labors, and his clothes deteriorate into tatters. Pat Conley follows him, tormenting him with information about the nature of his condition and her knowledge of his attraction to Wendy Wright. Joe struggles up the stairs in an agonizing effort, finally reaching his room. As he enters, Glen Runciter appears and sprays him with a can of Ubik, saving his life. Runciter explains that they are in cold-pac at the Beloved Brethren Moratorium in Zurich, that they have been there for a week, and that the deterioration is due to both normal half-life decay and an external attack. Joe realizes that Runciter has been trying to reach them from the outside world. The chapter reaches an emotional climax as Joe is literally saved from death by Ubik.

locations.name: Meremont Hotel lobby and second floor

themes: The approach of death and final persistence
The ambiguity of salvation and rescue
Malevolence and sadism in the face of weakness
The redemptive power of external intervention

theological_concepts.concept: Death as a trial that reveals character
Salvation through grace rather than earned merit
The existence of both demonic and divine forces in the afterlife
Resurrection and restoration through mysterious means

philosophical_concepts.concept: The nature of identity at the moment of dissolution
Free will and choice in the face of deterministic degradation
The problem of theodicy—why suffering is permitted
